(א) (s.k. 8) Permitted, etc., on account of wringing, etc. — even though in Beitzah 18a they said that according to all a person may immerse on Shabbat; and what is the reason — even for us who rule immersion at its time is not a mitzvah — nevertheless on account of tza'ar or mitzvat onah it is permitted and they were not concerned for these distant concerns; but when he could immerse before, the custom was stringent; and so Terumat HaDeshen wrote to be stringent, but for another reason:

(ב) Even though even Mordekhai, etc. — meaning we do not rule like Mordekhai, but in cold water it is permitted as written in seif 1; therefore he wrote "even for Mordekhai" — specifically in a vessel, because the observer thinks he washes in hot water; unlike in a river where everyone sees it is cold:

(ג) Nevertheless the custom is to forbid — for whatever reason; and it is possible on account of the concerns Maharil wrote — not on account of wringing alone but on account of those reasons to forbid washing alone; therefore even to immerse is forbidden, for it appears as fixing — meaning in the gemara they said: although a vessel that became impure is forbidden to immerse on Shabbat and Yom Tov because it is like fixing, a person may immerse because he appears as cooling himself even in rainy season and even in foul water; nevertheless sometimes he washes when his body is soiled with mud and excrement and washes to remove mud and excrement upon him — therefore he does not appear as fixing; if so, in our time where the custom is careful not to wash even in cold, as above — if a person immerses everyone knows it is for immersion and he will appear as fixing, and forbidden; and so in Yoreh De'ah siman 199 in name of Kol Bo, etc., on account of wringing hair — even though Rabbeinu Yehuda wrote there is no concern for this, for we rule there is no wringing in hair; therefore his intent is only not to push off mitzvah of immersion at its time; for even though Rambam wrote chapter 9 there is no wringing in hair from the Torah and therefore one is not liable for wringing hair — nevertheless its d'rabbanan prohibition exists, as written in siman 330; nevertheless he did not push off mitzvah of immersion at its time; but washing is certainly fit to forbid for this reason; and therefore immersion of mitzvah is also forbidden, for it appears as fixing — one cannot say he appears as cooling himself, for it is forbidden to immerse on account of wringing hair; since it is d'rabbanan it is not precise that even d'rabbanan there is none, for we rule immersion of a ba'al keri is voided; rather it is a general stringency, as written in siman 323 regarding immersing a new vessel on Shabbat — according to one who says vessel immersion is d'rabbanan, for one opinion it is permitted to immerse on Shabbat like immersing a vessel with impurity of the womb; since it is d'rabbanan, permitted to immerse on Shabbat and it is not called fixing; and the same here:

(ד) And in Agur, etc., that in a river it is forbidden — refers to above according to Terumat HaDeshen who wrote that in a river all permit; also in Beit Yosef in name of Kol Bo, etc. — these are duplicated words, for he already wrote thus above:

(ה) And it appears to me a mumar, etc. — for R' Yehuda, etc. — this is R' Yosi who holds he is not a convert until he circumcises and immerses; therefore even if he circumcised in our presence we do not immerse him on Shabbat because it is like fixing; but R' Yehuda holds one suffices — either circumcision or immersion, and in one his law is like an Israelite; therefore in any case both circumcision and immersion are needed, nevertheless in one of them it suffices for his law to be like an Israelite that his sanctified things are sanctified and he does not make yayin nesech, and for all matters he is like an Israelite; therefore if he circumcised in our presence we immerse him on Shabbat, for it is not like fixing; and we rule like R' Yosi; nevertheless from R' Yehuda we learn regarding immersion of a mumar who returned to Judaism that he requires immersion, as written at the end of siman 268 (and Taz siman 267 s.k. 5 wrote he also needs to shave) — meaning as a general stringency to liken him to a convert who converted; but from the law's side he need not at all, as the novellae wrote in Yevamos, for he is a full Israelite who was a wicked Israelite; and even though the novellae wrote d'rabbanan he needs immersion — not precise, for we do not find anywhere in the Talmud that a mumar who repented in responsa requires immersion; rather it is a stringency; and if so, he is no worse than a convert for R' Yehuda, who is permitted to immerse on Shabbat and it is not like fixing; and in Sefer Tashbetz he questioned this — all this is fine for the reason explained in the Talmud regarding a convert; but according to Rambam, and so Rabbeinu Yehuda cited there in Shulchan Aruch, who holds per the conclusion one need not the reason for prohibiting a convert's immersion on Shabbat as fixing, but he requires three for a convert's immersion as it is written regarding him "mishpat" and requires three like regarding mishpat — therefore we do not judge on Shabbat; if so this reason applies also to a mumar who repented, for we also require three at the time of immersion, as Rama wrote there; and in my humble opinion it is difficult: from the reason of mishpat he should not need Magen Avraham's reason to permit a mumar's immersion, for regarding a mumar "mishpat" is not written; and what we require three for his immersion is only for likeness like a convert; if so, certainly permitted on Shabbat — only nevertheless forbidden because it is fixing — where does this go, Magen Avraham wrote it is not fixing, as above:

cases.en_plain: (א) (s.k. 8) Permitted, etc., on account of wringing, etc. — even though in Beitzah 18a they said that according to all a person may immerse on Shabbat; and what is the reason — even for us who rule immersion at its time is not a mitzvah — nevertheless on account of tza'ar or mitzvat onah it is permitted and they were not concerned for these distant concerns; but when he could immerse before, the custom was stringent; and so Terumat HaDeshen wrote to be stringent, but for another reason: (ב) Even though even Mordekhai, etc. — meaning we do not rule like Mordekhai, but in cold water it is permitted as written in seif 1; therefore he wrote "even for Mordekhai" — specifically in a vessel, because the observer thinks he washes in hot water; unlike in a river where everyone sees it is cold: (ג) Nevertheless the custom is to forbid — for whatever reason; and it is possible on account of the concerns Maharil wrote — not on account of wringing alone but on account of those reasons to forbid washing alone; therefore even to immerse is forbidden, for it appears as fixing — meaning in the gemara they said: although a vessel that became impure is forbidden to immerse on Shabbat and Yom Tov because it is like fixing, a person may immerse because he appears as cooling himself even in rainy season and even in foul water; nevertheless sometimes he washes when his body is soiled with mud and excrement and washes to remove mud and excrement upon him — therefore he does not appear as fixing; if so, in our time where the custom is careful not to wash even in cold, as above — if a person immerses everyone knows it is for immersion and he will appear as fixing, and forbidden; and so in Yoreh De'ah siman 199 in name of Kol Bo, etc., on account of wringing hair — even though Rabbeinu Yehuda wrote there is no concern for this, for we rule there is no wringing in hair; therefore his intent is only not to push off mitzvah of immersion at its time; for even though Rambam wrote chapter 9 there is no wringing in hair from the Torah and therefore one is not liable for wringing hair — nevertheless its d'rabbanan prohibition exists, as written in siman 330; nevertheless he did not push off mitzvah of immersion at its time; but washing is certainly fit to forbid for this reason; and therefore immersion of mitzvah is also forbidden, for it appears as fixing — one cannot say he appears as cooling himself, for it is forbidden to immerse on account of wringing hair; since it is d'rabbanan it is not precise that even d'rabbanan there is none, for we rule immersion of a ba'al keri is voided; rather it is a general stringency, as written in siman 323 regarding immersing a new vessel on Shabbat — according to one who says vessel immersion is d'rabbanan, for one opinion it is permitted to immerse on Shabbat like immersing a vessel with impurity of the womb; since it is d'rabbanan, permitted to immerse on Shabbat and it is not called fixing; and the same here: (ד) And in Agur, etc., that in a river it is forbidden — refers to above according to Terumat HaDeshen who wrote that in a river all permit; also in Beit Yosef in name of Kol Bo, etc. — these are duplicated words, for he already wrote thus above: (ה) And it appears to me a mumar, etc. — for R' Yehuda, etc. — this is R' Yosi who holds he is not a convert until he circumcises and immerses; therefore even if he circumcised in our presence we do not immerse him on Shabbat because it is like fixing; but R' Yehuda holds one suffices — either circumcision or immersion, and in one his law is like an Israelite; therefore in any case both circumcision and immersion are needed, nevertheless in one of them it suffices for his law to be like an Israelite that his sanctified things are sanctified and he does not make yayin nesech, and for all matters he is like an Israelite; therefore if he circumcised in our presence we immerse him on Shabbat, for it is not like fixing; and we rule like R' Yosi; nevertheless from R' Yehuda we learn regarding immersion of a mumar who returned to Judaism that he requires immersion, as written at the end of siman 268 (and Taz siman 267 s.k. 5 wrote he also needs to shave) — meaning as a general stringency to liken him to a convert who converted; but from the law's side he need not at all, as the novellae wrote in Yevamos, for he is a full Israelite who was a wicked Israelite; and even though the novellae wrote d'rabbanan he needs immersion — not precise, for we do not find anywhere in the Talmud that a mumar who repented in responsa requires immersion; rather it is a stringency; and if so, he is no worse than a convert for R' Yehuda, who is permitted to immerse on Shabbat and it is not like fixing; and in Sefer Tashbetz he questioned this — all this is fine for the reason explained in the Talmud regarding a convert; but according to Rambam, and so Rabbeinu Yehuda cited there in Shulchan Aruch, who holds per the conclusion one need not the reason for prohibiting a convert's immersion on Shabbat as fixing, but he requires three for a convert's immersion as it is written regarding him "mishpat" and requires three like regarding mishpat — therefore we do not judge on Shabbat; if so this reason applies also to a mumar who repented, for we also require three at the time of immersion, as Rama wrote there; and in my humble opinion it is difficult: from the reason of mishpat he should not need Magen Avraham's reason to permit a mumar's immersion, for regarding a mumar "mishpat" is not written; and what we require three for his immersion is only for likeness like a convert; if so, certainly permitted on Shabbat — only nevertheless forbidden because it is fixing — where does this go, Magen Avraham wrote it is not fixing, as above:

NB: Behold this is agreed that pikuach nefesh overrides Shabbat, and the same for other negative commandments; and see in Chiddushei Torah parashat Emor year 5597 what I was uncertain there: whether several negative commandments together also override pikuach nefesh, or only one negative commandment is pushed aside for pikuach nefesh and not two negative commandments; and see there what I brought from gemara Yoma regarding feeding him the lighter, etc. And behold incidentally I will explain here the words of Rosh in chapter 8 of Yoma section 14 that are wondrous, thus: they asked Raavad: a sick person with danger, etc., and he answered the words of "some say" are intended [for another case], but one could say that since the prohibition of Shabbat was already given to be pushed aside for kindling and cooking and heating water for him — thus it is impossible there not be one minor at the end of the world, etc. And behold this "or also" has no understanding; and I saw in responsum Chasam Sofer Orach Chayim part 1 siman 25 who strained to explain the intent regarding a minor to circumcise him, and this explanation is not tolerable at all, for then it should have said it is impossible there not be one circumcised today. Therefore it appears in my humble opinion: since we establish regarding a minor who slaughtered and others see him — his slaughter is valid; and since we establish a minor eats neveilot — bet din is not commanded to separate him, only by hand it is forbidden to give him. And behold it appears from gemara Yevamot daf 114, where it says do not feed him by hand — it is proven specifically by hand it is forbidden to give, but to tell him by mouth is permitted; and even if we say also by mouth forbidden to tell him — see in Kinnat Sofrim at its end. Nevertheless it appears this is only rabbinically, and from the Torah permitted to tell him at least by mouth; and thus since if there were a minor here it would be permitted to slaughter through a minor — thus slaughter has permission for its prohibition through a minor; but neveilah for eating — there is no permission to give a person to eat except through pushing aside; therefore better to slaughter for him; and see similar reasoning in Beit Yosef on Tur Orach Chayim siman 11, who wrote that what we establish "if impossible to fulfill both" — a positive commandment overrides a negative commandment — this is specifically when impossible in any manner to fulfill both through permission; but if possible in some manner, even though now impossible, it does not override. Behold what is possible sometime to fulfill through permission, even though now impossible, is considered possible; one could say likewise regarding a sick person it is the reverse: since it is possible sometime through a minor, it is considered possible through permission; therefore it is lighter than a matter impossible in any manner to be through permission; examine.

הולד שנולד וכו' - המג"א כתב דבכולהו יש להו צער וכיון דכל אלה אינם מלאכה לא גזרו בהו רבנן והוא מתוספות שילהי פרק מפנין ובשאלתות דרב אחאי פרשת שמות משמע דמניעת חתוך הטבור יכול להיות סכנה לולד דז"ל שם מהו לחתוך טבור בשבת וכו' כי קא מיבעי לי בחד ולד מי אמרינן אפשר לאזדהורי [היינו בקשירת הטבור לבד] ולא אתי לידי סכנה או דילמא זימנין דלאו אדעתיה ואתי לידי סכנה או דלמא הלכה כר' יוסי דמסתבר טעמיה דזמנין דמנתח והוי ספק נפשות וס"נ להקל ופשיט ממימרא דר"נ דהלכה כר' יוסי וכ"כ חידושי הר"ן שם במתניתין דאם לא יחתכנו איכא סכנתא עי"ש וכ"כ המאירי במשנה שם וברמב"ם פ"ב מהלכות שבת מבואר ביותר מזה שהוא כלל בסכנה את כל אלו הדברים אם ימנע מהולד שאחר שחשב בהלכה י"א הדברים שעושין לולד סיים ע"ז מפני שסכנה הוא לו אם לא יעשו לו כל אלה ולפ"ז דבר פשוט הוא דאפילו במלאכה דאורייתא מחללינן היכי דא"א בענין אחר ואין כונת הש"ס בהני מלאכות מפני שהם מדרבנן דבאמת עושים אותם ביום שנולד אפילו היכא דקעביד איסור דאורייתא על ידם כגון להחם חמין כדי לרחוץ או כדי לשחק הסימנין הצריכין לו למליחה או גבי מלפפים לחתך בגד לעשות חותלות או להביא סכין דרך ר"ה לחתוך הטבור [חוץ מטמינת שליא דאסור לטמון בארץ משום דאינו אלא סגולה וכמו שכתב המאירי והרמב"ם השמיטה בחבורו] וכונת הרמב"ם שם במה שכתב בחמין שהוחמו בשבת היינו אפילו אם הוחמו ע"י ישראל [עיין בפ"ב מהלכות מילה בשאלת חכמי לוניל ובתשובתו שם] [הג"ה ודע דבדברי הרמב"ם אלו דמשמע מיניה דללפף להולד יש חשש סכנתא אם ימנעו מזה יתיישב מאד מימרא דר"נ דקאמר מכאן שמלפפים להולד הנולד והלא קאמר בדף ס"ו לפופי ינוקי בשבתא שפיר דמי הרי דבכל שבת שרי [ועיין לקמן מה שכתבנו ע"ז בשם שארי ראשונים] ואין בזה משום שבות כלל ומאי רבותא הכא אבל לפי הרמב"ם ניחא דשם אשמעינן הגמרא דמשום דיהיה בזה צער אם ימנע לכך לא גזרו רבנן וכן דייק הרמב"ם בפרק כ"א מהלכות שבת דין ל"א עי"ש וכאן אשמועינן הגמרא דביום שנולד הליפוף הוא מכלל שאר צרכי הכרח להולד ונ"מ דמותר לעבור אמלאכה דאורייתא בשביל זה] ועכ"פ נראה פשוט דיש להקל לכתחלה להחם חמין ע"י עו"ג כדי לרחוץ התינוק וכמו שכתבתי במ"ב ואח"כ מצאתי בספר נזר ישראל בשם שו"ת שו"מ שכתב ג"כ הכי:
או ספק בן זיין - דין זה העתיק המחבר מהטור וכפי הנראה הוא כמו שכתב הב"י דמקורו הוא מהא דשבת קל"ה בברייתא בן שבעה מחללים עליו וכו' ובן ח' אין מחללין עליו ספק בן זיי"ן או בן חי"ת אין מחללים בן חי"ת הרי הוא כאבן וכו' ומפרש הטור דכונת הברייתא לענין חילול שבת ממש לרפאותו ולהחיותו דאם היה מפרש דהברייתא מיירי לענין למולו בשבת לא היה מדייק מזה דאין מחללין דמילה לא מהלינן מספיקא ביום השבת אבל חילול שבת לרפואה מחללינן מספיקא כדקי"ל בנפל גל ספק חי ספק מת מפקחין ולכאורה הלא בגמרא שם מוכח דהברייתא אמילה קאי וכן פירש"י שם וי"ל דגם הטור מודה לזה אלא דסובר דברייתא כוללת שניהם מדקאמר שם לישנא דסתם חלול ואין להקשות בדף ל"ו דקמותיב מהאי ברייתא לימהליה ממ"נ והוצרך לאוקמי' במכשירי מילה ואליבא דר"א יותר הו"ל לאוקמיה לענין חלול שבת ממש לבד וכפשטיה דלישנא דברייתא א"ו דס"ל להגמרא דהברייתא לענין מילה מתנייא וי"ל דאי הוה מתרץ ליה כן הוי מקשה ליה מברייתא קמייתא דאמר שם ערלתו ודאי דוחה את השבת ולא ספק דוחה את השבת אכן מדברי הרמב"ם שלא העתיק דין זה רק בהלכות מילה משמע דסובר דברייתא זו רק לענין מילה מתנייא והנה בבה"ג הלכות מילה לענין ספק בן חי"ת כתב בהדיא ולענין אחולי שבתא מחללינן מספיקא דקאמרינן כל ספק נפשות להקל וגם העיטור בהלכות מילה מביא דבריו לפסק הלכה וכפי הנראה שם גם רב האי גאון כתב כן והעיטור לא פליג עליו שם כ"א הוסיף דהיכי דגמרו צפרניו אפילו פירש ממנה תיכף גם זה בכלל ספק דאמרינן אשתהויי אשתהי וכן המאירי שם בדף קל"ו כתב ג"כ ככל דברי בה"ג וכתב אמנם לענין לחלל שבת כו"ע מודו דמחללין עי"ש וכן בספר האשכול כשהעתיק הברייתא דספק בן זיי"ן אין מחללים כתב ע"ז וז"ל פי' למולו ור"ל דלא נטעה לפרש דקאי על כל חלול ואולם יש לדחות דאפשר דהם מיירי היכי דגמרו שערו וצפרניו [וכן משמע קצת בעיטור שם עי"ש] אבל היכא דלא גמרו יותר מסתבר לומר דהוא בן חי"ת. והנה מסוגיא דערכין בישבה על המשבר ומתה והובא בס"ה דמקילינן מספיקא להביא סכין דרך ר"ה תירץ המגן אברהם דהתם מיירי שידעינן שכלו חדשיו והנה עוד מביא המגן אברהם שתלוי זה בשני תירוצים שהובא בתה"א להרמב"ן לענין עוברה שהריחה דלתירוץ א' שהם דברי הבה"ג מבואר שגם בולד קודם מ' יום דמיא בעלמא הוא אעפ"כ מחללים וא"כ כ"ש בנולד לאויר העולם והוא ספק דמחללין אך לפי מה שביאר שם הרמב"ן הטעם ביושבת על המשבר דחשוב כילוד ורק הדלת ננעל בפניו א"כ עכ"פ נאמר דדוקא דכלו לו חדשיו עי"ש [והנה לפי דברי המגן אברהם זה ממילא נדחה הראיה שהבאנו לעיל מבה"ג דאפשר דהוא אזיל לשיטתיה בזה דסבר דמחללין אפילו על עוברין וכ"ש שם] ולענ"ד לא תלוי כלל זה בזה דאפילו לפי תירוץ זה לא קאמר שם הרמב"ן רק דבעוברין לא מחללין משום דישראל אינו מצווה על העוברין ויושבת על המשבר לא מיקרי עוברין וכנולד דמיא משא"כ בנולד אפשר דגם הרמב"ן מודה דאע"ג דאין נהרגין עליו מספיקא משום ושפטו העדה וגו' אעפ"כ מחללין מספיקא דספק נפשות להקל ולהיפך ג"כ קצת יש לדחות דהתם אם נאכיל לאמו ביוה"כ מסתמא לבסוף תלד בן קיימא וישמור שבתות הרבה ולכך התירה התורה וכמש"כ הר"ן משא"כ בזה שכבר נולד וחזינן שלא גמרו שערו וצפרניו מסתברא שהוא בן חי"ת ולא יחיה ולמה נחלל שבת עליה. ודע דלדברי המגן אברהם הנ"ל דתלוי זה בשני התירוצים ממילא לפי מה שפסק הריטב"א בחידושי נדה ד' מ"ד כדעת הבה"ג דאפילו על עובר מחללינן ממילא מחללינן גם על ספק בן חי"ת:

(א) The newborn who was born, etc. — Magen Avraham wrote that in all of them there is distress; and since all these are not melacha they did not decree on them — and this is from Tosafos at the end of chapter Mefanin and in She'eilotot of Rav Achai parashat Shemos it implies that preventing cutting the cord can be danger to the infant — end of his words there: what about cutting the cord on Shabbat, etc., for I ask regarding one fetus — do we say perhaps he can be careful [meaning tying the cord alone] and danger will not come, or perhaps sometimes unawares danger comes, or perhaps the halacha is like R' Yosi whose reason is plausible that sometimes it tears and it is doubt of life-threatening danger and doubt is resolved leniently; and he concludes from R' Nachman's statement that halacha is like R' Yosi; and so Ran's chiddushim there, in the mishnah — if they do not cut it there is danger — see there; and so Meiri in the mishnah there; and in Rambam chapter 2 of Hilchot Shabbat it is explained more than this that it is a general rule in danger for all these matters — if they prevent the newborn, after he considered in halacha 11 the matters done for the newborn he concluded because it is danger to him if they do not do all these for him; and accordingly it is obvious that even in d'oraisa melacha they desecrate when impossible another way; and the intent of the gemara in these melachot is not because they are d'rabbanan — for in truth they do them on the day he is born even where d'oraisa prohibition is done through them, such as heating hot water to wash or to salt the signs needed for salting, or regarding lefofei to cut cloth for swaddling, or to bring a knife through public domain to cut the cord [except burying placenta — forbidden to bury in earth because it is only a segulah, as Meiri wrote and Rambam omitted in his composition]; and Rambam's intent there in what he wrote in hot water that was heated on Shabbat — even if heated through Israelite [see chapter 2 of Hilchot Milah in She'eilot of Lunil scholars and his responsum there] [gloss: and know that in Rambam's words these that imply lefofei for the newborn there is concern of danger if they prevent — this settles very well R' Nachman's statement that from here they lefofei for the newborn who was born; but behold it says on daf 66 lefofei infants on Shabbat is fine — behold on every Shabbat permitted [and see below what we wrote on this in the name of other early authorities]; and there is no shvus matter at all — what is the novelty here; but according to Rambam it is fine, for there the gemara informs us that because there will be distress if they prevent, therefore the Rabbis did not decree; and so Rambam infers in chapter 21 of Hilchot Shabbat halacha 41 — see there; and here the gemara informs us that on the day he is born lefofei is among other essential needs of the newborn; and the difference is that it is permitted to transgress d'oraisa melacha for this]. And in any case it appears obvious one should be lenient l'chatchila to heat hot water through non-Jew to wash the infant; and as I wrote in Mishna Berurah; and afterward I found in Sefer Nazer Yisrael in the name of responsum of Shevut Yaakov he also wrote so.

(ב) Or doubt seven-month, etc. — This law the Mechaber copied from Tur; and as it appears its source is as Beit Yosef wrote — from that which Shabbos 135 baraita: seven-month they desecrate for him, etc.; eight-month they do not desecrate; doubt seven-month or eight-month they do not desecrate; eight-month — behold he is like a stone, etc.; and Tur explains the baraita's intent is regarding actual Shabbat desecration to heal and sustain him — for if he explained the baraita deals regarding circumcision on Shabbat he would not infer from this that they do not desecrate, for from doubt we do not circumcise on Shabbat day; but for Shabbat desecration for healing we desecrate from doubt as we rule in fallen wall — doubt alive doubt dead we clear away; and apparently in the gemara there it is proven the baraita refers to circumcision, and so Rashi there; and one can say Tur also agrees, only he holds the baraita includes both from that which it says there general desecration language; and one cannot ask on daf 36 that challenges from this baraita to circumcise in any case, and needed to establish it regarding facilitators of circumcision and according to R' Eliezer more — it would have been better to establish it regarding actual Shabbat desecration alone per the baraita's plain language; or that the gemara holds the baraita is taught regarding circumcision; and one can say if he had answered so he would challenge from the first baraita that says there his foreskin, etc., certainly pushes aside Shabbat and not doubt pushes aside Shabbat; but from Rambam who did not copy this law only in Hilchot Milah it implies he holds this baraita is taught only regarding circumcision. And behold in Behag laws of milah regarding doubt eight-month he wrote explicitly: and regarding permitting Shabbat we desecrate from doubt, for we say all doubt of life-threatening danger is resolved leniently; and also Ittur in laws of milah brings his words for halachic ruling; and as it appears there Rav Hai Gaon also wrote so; and Ittur did not argue there only added that where nails were completed even if one separated from it immediately — also this is within doubt, for it remained; and so Meiri there on daf 136 also wrote as all Behag's words; and he wrote: however regarding desecrating Shabbat all agree they desecrate — see there; and so in Sefer HaEshkol when he copied the baraita doubt seven-month they do not desecrate he wrote on this — end of his words: explanation — to circumcise him; meaning they did not intend to explain it refers to all desecration; but one can reject that perhaps they deal where hair and nails were completed [and so it appears somewhat in Ittur there — see there]; but where they were not completed it is more reasonable to say he is eight-month. And behold from the sugya in Erchin 'she sat on the birth-stool and died' brought in Sefer HaHashlamah — we are lenient from doubt to bring knife through public domain — Magen Avraham answered that there it deals when we know her months were completed; and further Magen Avraham brings this depends on two answers brought in Torat HaAdam to Ramban regarding her fetus that smelled — for answer one, Behag's words are clear that even for newborn before forty days it is mere water — nevertheless they desecrate; if so all the more for one born to the world; and he is doubt that they desecrate; but according to what Ramban explained there the reason for one sitting on birth-stool — she is considered like birth and only the door is locked before him — if so at least we say specifically when her months were completed — see there [and behold according to Magen Avraham's words this is automatically rejected — perhaps he goes according to Behag there that he holds they desecrate even for fetuses, and all the more there]; and in my humble opinion this does not depend on this at all — for even according to this answer Ramban did not say there only that for fetuses they do not desecrate because Israel is not commanded regarding fetuses; and one sitting on birth-stool is not called fetuses; and like newborn it is water — not so for newborn perhaps Ramban also agrees that although they are not executed on him from doubt because of 'and the congregation shall judge,' etc., nevertheless they desecrate from doubt because doubt of life-threatening danger is resolved leniently; and conversely one can also reject somewhat — for there if they feed his mother on Yom Kippur presumptively she will eventually give birth a viable son who will observe many Shabbats, therefore the Torah permitted; as Ran wrote — not so here who was already born and we see hair and nails were not completed — it is reasonable he is eight-month and why desecrate Shabbat for him. And know that according to Magen Avraham above who said this depends on the two answers — from this Ritva in chiddushim of Niddah 4:44 as Behag's view — even for fetus they desecrate — from this they desecrate also for doubt eight-month.

ואין כונת הש"ס בהני מלאכות מפני שהם מדרבנן דבאמת עושים אותם ביום שנולד אפילו היכא דקעביד איסור דאורייתא על ידם כגון להחם חמין כדי לרחוץ או כדי לשחק הסימנין הצריכין לו למליחה או גבי מלפפים לחתך בגד לעשות חותלות או להביא סכין דרך ר"ה לחתוך הטבור [חוץ מטמינת שליא דאסור לטמון בארץ משום דאינו אלא סגולה וכמו שכתב המאירי והרמב"ם השמיטה בחבורו] וכונת הרמב"ם שם במה שכתב בחמין שהוחמו בשבת היינו אפילו אם הוחמו ע"י ישראל [עיין בפ"ב מהלכות מילה בשאלת חכמי לוניל ובתשובתו שם] [הג"ה ודע דבדברי הרמב"ם אלו דמשמע מיניה דללפף להולד יש חשש סכנתא אם ימנעו מזה יתיישב מאד מימרא דר"נ דקאמר מכאן שמלפפים להולד הנולד והלא קאמר בדף ס"ו לפופי ינוקי בשבתא שפיר דמי הרי דבכל שבת שרי [ועיין לקמן מה שכתבנו ע"ז בשם שארי ראשונים] ואין בזה משום שבות כלל ומאי רבותא הכא אבל לפי הרמב"ם ניחא דשם אשמעינן הגמרא דמשום דיהיה בזה צער אם ימנע לכך לא גזרו רבנן וכן דייק הרמב"ם בפרק כ"א מהלכות שבת דין ל"א עי"ש וכאן אשמועינן הגמרא דביום שנולד הליפוף הוא מכלל שאר צרכי הכרח להולד ונ"מ דמותר לעבור אמלאכה דאורייתא בשביל זה] ועכ"פ נראה פשוט דיש להקל לכתחלה להחם חמין ע"י עו"ג כדי לרחוץ התינוק וכמו שכתבתי במ"ב ואח"כ מצאתי בספר נזר ישראל בשם שו"ת שו"מ שכתב ג"כ הכי: או ספק בן זיין - דין זה העתיק המחבר מהטור וכפי הנראה הוא כמו שכתב הב"י דמקורו הוא מהא דשבת קל"ה בברייתא בן שבעה מחללים עליו וכו' ובן ח' אין מחללין עליו ספק בן זיי"ן או בן חי"ת אין מחללים בן חי"ת הרי הוא כאבן וכו' ומפרש הטור דכונת הברייתא לענין חילול שבת ממש לרפאותו ולהחיותו דאם היה מפרש דהברייתא מיירי לענין למולו בשבת לא היה מדייק מזה דאין מחללין דמילה לא מהלינן מספיקא ביום השבת אבל חילול שבת לרפואה מחללינן מספיקא כדקי"ל בנפל גל ספק חי ספק מת מפקחין ולכאורה הלא בגמרא שם מוכח דהברייתא אמילה קאי וכן פירש"י שם וי"ל דגם הטור מודה לזה אלא דסובר דברייתא כוללת שניהם מדקאמר שם לישנא דסתם חלול ואין להקשות בדף ל"ו דקמותיב מהאי ברייתא לימהליה ממ"נ והוצרך לאוקמי' במכשירי מילה ואליבא דר"א יותר הו"ל לאוקמיה לענין חלול שבת ממש לבד וכפשטיה דלישנא דברייתא א"ו דס"ל להגמרא דהברייתא לענין מילה מתנייא וי"ל דאי הוה מתרץ ליה כן הוי מקשה ליה מברייתא קמייתא דאמר שם ערלתו ודאי דוחה את השבת ולא ספק דוחה את השבת אכן מדברי הרמב"ם שלא העתיק דין זה רק בהלכות מילה משמע דסובר דברייתא זו רק לענין מילה מתנייא והנה בבה"ג הלכות מילה לענין ספק בן חי"ת כתב בהדיא ולענין אחולי שבתא מחללינן מספיקא דקאמרינן כל ספק נפשות להקל וגם העיטור בהלכות מילה מביא דבריו לפסק הלכה וכפי הנראה שם גם רב האי גאון כתב כן והעיטור לא פליג עליו שם כ"א הוסיף דהיכי דגמרו צפרניו אפילו פירש ממנה תיכף גם זה בכלל ספק דאמרינן אשתהויי אשתהי וכן המאירי שם בדף קל"ו כתב ג"כ ככל דברי בה"ג וכתב אמנם לענין לחלל שבת כו"ע מודו דמחללין עי"ש וכן בספר האשכול כשהעתיק הברייתא דספק בן זיי"ן אין מחללים כתב ע"ז וז"ל פי' למולו ור"ל דלא נטעה לפרש דקאי על כל חלול ואולם יש לדחות דאפשר דהם מיירי היכי דגמרו שערו וצפרניו [וכן משמע קצת בעיטור שם עי"ש] אבל היכא דלא גמרו יותר מסתבר לומר דהוא בן חי"ת. והנה מסוגיא דערכין בישבה על המשבר ומתה והובא בס"ה דמקילינן מספיקא להביא סכין דרך ר"ה תירץ המגן אברהם דהתם מיירי שידעינן שכלו חדשיו והנה עוד מביא המגן אברהם שתלוי זה בשני תירוצים שהובא בתה"א להרמב"ן לענין עוברה שהריחה דלתירוץ א' שהם דברי הבה"ג מבואר שגם בולד קודם מ' יום דמיא בעלמא הוא אעפ"כ מחללים וא"כ כ"ש בנולד לאויר העולם והוא ספק דמחללין אך לפי מה שביאר שם הרמב"ן הטעם ביושבת על המשבר דחשוב כילוד ורק הדלת ננעל בפניו א"כ עכ"פ נאמר דדוקא דכלו לו חדשיו עי"ש [והנה לפי דברי המגן אברהם זה ממילא נדחה הראיה שהבאנו לעיל מבה"ג דאפשר דהוא אזיל לשיטתיה בזה דסבר דמחללין אפילו על עוברין וכ"ש שם] ולענ"ד לא תלוי כלל זה בזה דאפילו לפי תירוץ זה לא קאמר שם הרמב"ן רק דבעוברין לא מחללין משום דישראל אינו מצווה על העוברין ויושבת על המשבר לא מיקרי עוברין וכנולד דמיא משא"כ בנולד אפשר דגם הרמב"ן מודה דאע"ג דאין נהרגין עליו מספיקא משום ושפטו העדה וגו' אעפ"כ מחללין מספיקא דספק נפשות להקל ולהיפך ג"כ קצת יש לדחות דהתם אם נאכיל לאמו ביוה"כ מסתמא לבסוף תלד בן קיימא וישמור שבתות הרבה ולכך התירה התורה וכמש"כ הר"ן משא"כ בזה שכבר נולד וחזינן שלא גמרו שערו וצפרניו מסתברא שהוא בן חי"ת ולא יחיה ולמה נחלל שבת עליה. ודע דלדברי המגן אברהם הנ"ל דתלוי זה בשני התירוצים ממילא לפי מה שפסק הריטב"א בחידושי נדה ד' מ"ד כדעת הבה"ג דאפילו על עובר מחללינן ממילא מחללינן גם על ספק בן חי"ת:
cases.en_plain: (א) The newborn who was born, etc. — Magen Avraham wrote that in all of them there is distress; and since all these are not melacha they did not decree on them — and this is from Tosafos at the end of chapter Mefanin and in She'eilotot of Rav Achai parashat Shemos it implies that preventing cutting the cord can be danger to the infant — end of his words there: what about cutting the cord on Shabbat, etc., for I ask regarding one fetus — do we say perhaps he can be careful [meaning tying the cord alone] and danger will not come, or perhaps sometimes unawares danger comes, or perhaps the halacha is like R' Yosi whose reason is plausible that sometimes it tears and it is doubt of life-threatening danger and doubt is resolved leniently; and he concludes from R' Nachman's statement that halacha is like R' Yosi; and so Ran's chiddushim there, in the mishnah — if they do not cut it there is danger — see there; and so Meiri in the mishnah there; and in Rambam chapter 2 of Hilchot Shabbat it is explained more than this that it is a general rule in danger for all these matters — if they prevent the newborn, after he considered in halacha 11 the matters done for the newborn he concluded because it is danger to him if they do not do all these for him; and accordingly it is obvious that even in d'oraisa melacha they desecrate when impossible another way; and the intent of the gemara in these melachot is not because they are d'rabbanan — for in truth they do them on the day he is born even where d'oraisa prohibition is done through them, such as heating hot water to wash or to salt the signs needed for salting, or regarding lefofei to cut cloth for swaddling, or to bring a knife through public domain to cut the cord [except burying placenta — forbidden to bury in earth because it is only a segulah, as Meiri wrote and Rambam omitted in his composition]; and Rambam's intent there in what he wrote in hot water that was heated on Shabbat — even if heated through Israelite [see chapter 2 of Hilchot Milah in She'eilot of Lunil scholars and his responsum there] [gloss: and know that in Rambam's words these that imply lefofei for the newborn there is concern of danger if they prevent — this settles very well R' Nachman's statement that from here they lefofei for the newborn who was born; but behold it says on daf 66 lefofei infants on Shabbat is fine — behold on every Shabbat permitted [and see below what we wrote on this in the name of other early authorities]; and there is no shvus matter at all — what is the novelty here; but according to Rambam it is fine, for there the gemara informs us that because there will be distress if they prevent, therefore the Rabbis did not decree; and so Rambam infers in chapter 21 of Hilchot Shabbat halacha 41 — see there; and here the gemara informs us that on the day he is born lefofei is among other essential needs of the newborn; and the difference is that it is permitted to transgress d'oraisa melacha for this]. And in any case it appears obvious one should be lenient l'chatchila to heat hot water through non-Jew to wash the infant; and as I wrote in Mishna Berurah; and afterward I found in Sefer Nazer Yisrael in the name of responsum of Shevut Yaakov he also wrote so. (ב) Or doubt seven-month, etc. — This law the Mechaber copied from Tur; and as it appears its source is as Beit Yosef wrote — from that which Shabbos 135 baraita: seven-month they desecrate for him, etc.; eight-month they do not desecrate; doubt seven-month or eight-month they do not desecrate; eight-month — behold he is like a stone, etc.; and Tur explains the baraita's intent is regarding actual Shabbat desecration to heal and sustain him — for if he explained the baraita deals regarding circumcision on Shabbat he would not infer from this that they do not desecrate, for from doubt we do not circumcise on Shabbat day; but for Shabbat desecration for healing we desecrate from doubt as we rule in fallen wall — doubt alive doubt dead we clear away; and apparently in the gemara there it is proven the baraita refers to circumcision, and so Rashi there; and one can say Tur also agrees, only he holds the baraita includes both from that which it says there general desecration language; and one cannot ask on daf 36 that challenges from this baraita to circumcise in any case, and needed to establish it regarding facilitators of circumcision and according to R' Eliezer more — it would have been better to establish it regarding actual Shabbat desecration alone per the baraita's plain language; or that the gemara holds the baraita is taught regarding circumcision; and one can say if he had answered so he would challenge from the first baraita that says there his foreskin, etc., certainly pushes aside Shabbat and not doubt pushes aside Shabbat; but from Rambam who did not copy this law only in Hilchot Milah it implies he holds this baraita is taught only regarding circumcision. And behold in Behag laws of milah regarding doubt eight-month he wrote explicitly: and regarding permitting Shabbat we desecrate from doubt, for we say all doubt of life-threatening danger is resolved leniently; and also Ittur in laws of milah brings his words for halachic ruling; and as it appears there Rav Hai Gaon also wrote so; and Ittur did not argue there only added that where nails were completed even if one separated from it immediately — also this is within doubt, for it remained; and so Meiri there on daf 136 also wrote as all Behag's words; and he wrote: however regarding desecrating Shabbat all agree they desecrate — see there; and so in Sefer HaEshkol when he copied the baraita doubt seven-month they do not desecrate he wrote on this — end of his words: explanation — to circumcise him; meaning they did not intend to explain it refers to all desecration; but one can reject that perhaps they deal where hair and nails were completed [and so it appears somewhat in Ittur there — see there]; but where they were not completed it is more reasonable to say he is eight-month. And behold from the sugya in Erchin 'she sat on the birth-stool and died' brought in Sefer HaHashlamah — we are lenient from doubt to bring knife through public domain — Magen Avraham answered that there it deals when we know her months were completed; and further Magen Avraham brings this depends on two answers brought in Torat HaAdam to Ramban regarding her fetus that smelled — for answer one, Behag's words are clear that even for newborn before forty days it is mere water — nevertheless they desecrate; if so all the more for one born to the world; and he is doubt that they desecrate; but according to what Ramban explained there the reason for one sitting on birth-stool — she is considered like birth and only the door is locked before him — if so at least we say specifically when her months were completed — see there [and behold according to Magen Avraham's words this is automatically rejected — perhaps he goes according to Behag there that he holds they desecrate even for fetuses, and all the more there]; and in my humble opinion this does not depend on this at all — for even according to this answer Ramban did not say there only that for fetuses they do not desecrate because Israel is not commanded regarding fetuses; and one sitting on birth-stool is not called fetuses; and like newborn it is water — not so for newborn perhaps Ramban also agrees that although they are not executed on him from doubt because of 'and the congregation shall judge,' etc., nevertheless they desecrate from doubt because doubt of life-threatening danger is resolved leniently; and conversely one can also reject somewhat — for there if they feed his mother on Yom Kippur presumptively she will eventually give birth a viable son who will observe many Shabbats, therefore the Torah permitted; as Ran wrote — not so here who was already born and we see hair and nails were not completed — it is reasonable he is eight-month and why desecrate Shabbat for him. And know that according to Magen Avraham above who said this depends on the two answers — from this Ritva in chiddushim of Niddah 4:44 as Behag's view — even for fetus they desecrate — from this they desecrate also for doubt eight-month.
